name: Australia

C.evidence: Solid, noisy travelling support (Green and Gold Army), big crowds for key home qualifiers; football is not the national first sport and home matches rotate around rugby/cricket grounds.

V.evidence: No FIFA discrimination or crowd sanctions in the 2026 cycle. The 2022 squad published a video on migrant-worker rights and same-sex marriage before Qatar; First Nations-designed kit; heavy investment in the Matildas.

H.evidence: Seven World Cups, six in a row; 2006 Hiddink run, 2015 Asian Cup, the only team to win two confederation titles; round-of-32 run in 2026 after beating Turkey 2-0.

O.evidence: Football Australia is a member-based body without government ties; recurring financial pressure and a volatile A-League, but no corruption findings.

S.evidence: Tony Popovic (since Sept 2024) built an intense, hard-running side that beat Turkey and took Egypt to penalties; young squad (Irankunda, Metcalfe) with a strong team-fan bond; Mat Ryan long-serving captain.

wc2026: round of 32 (Group D: W1 D1 L1; lost to Egypt on penalties after 1-1)

name: Iran

C.evidence: Azadi Stadium crowds are among Asia's loudest and a large diaspora follows Team Melli; support is politically split since 2022 (protest symbols in the stands); women largely excluded from domestic stadiums for decades.

V.evidence: Federation objected to the Seattle 'Pride Match' vs Egypt; long-running ban on women in stadiums; players who showed solidarity with protesters (2022 anthem, 2026 massacres) faced state pressure.

H.evidence: Seven World Cups but never past the group stage; famous 1998 win over the United States; three straight Asian Cups (1968-76); Ali Daei's scoring record.

O.evidence: Football Federation Islamic Republic of Iran is controlled by the state (Ministry of Sport appointments); FIFA suspended it in 2006 over government interference.

S.evidence: Amir Ghalenoei (second spell) with an experienced, stable core (Taremi, Hajsafi 149 caps); three draws in 2026 but eliminated; squad bond with fans strained by politics.

adjustments.evidence: Freedom House 2026: 10/100, Not Free; RSF 2026 rank 177 of 180; 2026 massacres of protesters including athletes.

name: Japan

C.evidence: Ultras Nippon lead a loud, organised singing section and a large travelling following; world-known for cleaning the stands; atmosphere is committed rather than volcanic.

V.evidence: Exemplary conduct: no red card at any World Cup since 1998, fans' stadium clean-ups, no FIFA sanctions; strong investment in the women's team (2011 world champions); clear youth pathway.

H.evidence: Eight straight World Cups; wins over Germany and Spain in 2022; record four Asian Cups; the J.League development model is widely copied.

O.evidence: Japan Football Association is independent and transparent, runs a long-term published plan ('Japan's Way'); stable coach contract policy.

S.evidence: Hajime Moriyasu in charge since 2018, a defining long-serving coach; high-press, high-work-rate side with a stable core; round of 32 in 2026 (lost 2-1 to Brazil).

name: Cape Verde

name: DR Congo

C.evidence: Passionate Leopards support and big diaspora; the government declared a public holiday after qualification; strong following at AFCON 2023 and in the US.

O.evidence: FECOFA is heavily state-funded; former president Constant Omari was arrested in 2021 over embezzlement of public funds.

S.evidence: Sebastien Desabre in charge since 2022 (AFCON 2023 semi-final, qualification through two play-off rounds); captain Chancel Mbemba 114 caps; intense, well-organised side that led England in the round of 32.

adjustments.evidence: Freedom House 2026: 18/100, Not Free; RSF 2025 rank 133; armed conflict in the east.

S.evidence: Hossam Hassan (since 2024) built the best Egypt World Cup run; captain Salah is the icon; stable core.

adjustments.evidence: Freedom House 2026: 18/100, Not Free; RSF 2026 rank 169.
